subject: Linguistics
title: Abugidas
description: A micro-lesson that makes Abugidas usable.

hook.text: In Devanagari, each symbol is a consonant with a built-in 'a' vowel—change the vowel with a mark.

buildup.text: An abugida represents consonant-vowel units, with the vowel modified by diacritical marks.

discovery.text: Most South and Southeast Asian scripts are abugidas—Thai, Tibetan, Khmer, and Ethiopic.

twist.text: The default vowel doesn't need marking—only non-default vowels get extra symbols.

climax.text: Abugidas balance information density with readability—more compact than alphabets, simpler than syllabaries.

punchline.text: One base plus a modification—vowels ride on consonants.

quiz.question: How does an abugida handle vowels?
options: A default vowel is inherent; others are marked
